editorial.headline: Nationally Open, Bali-Blocked: Non-Motorised Passenger Transport
editorial.standfirst: This passenger-transport activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, but PMA registration in Bali is blocked by the province’s permanent risk-based moratorium.
editorial.body:
This activity is about moving passengers without a motor. Its practical territory spans horse-drawn carriages—delman, bendi, andong and dokar—alongside becak, bicycle-taxi rides and the rental of non-motorised passenger vehicles. It is a specific passenger-transport category, not a catch-all for every vehicle without an engine: passenger transport within tourist areas and transport of goods are outside its stated scope. The distinction matters because the activity is defined by the journey offered to a passenger, whether the operator supplies a ride or hires out a non-motorised vehicle for that purpose. The names in the scope make clear that both passenger rides and non-motorised passenger rental belong here when they remain within that stated field.

The registration profile is broad on business scale. The record opens it to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises, so the classification is not confined to a small informal operation or a particular business size. Every one of the four listed scales is included. Nationally, it is TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a maximum foreign ownership of 100%. In plain terms, the national setting permits full foreign ownership; no lower foreign-equity cap is stated in the record. Its national reference is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021.

Bali changes the answer decisively. A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today. The recorded Bali status is a block grounded in risk class: in OSS, the Besar-scale assessment across every scope is Low or Medium-Low risk. That places the activity within Bali’s island-wide, permanent moratorium on PMA registration where the recorded risk class is Low or Medium-Low. The moratorium is attributed to Gubernur letter B.27.000/642/PM/DPMPTSP, and the recorded reason dates the block to May 2026.

This is not a qualification of the national 100% ceiling; it is a different local registration outcome. At the national level, full foreign ownership is allowed. In Bali, the same foreign-investment route is blocked by the provincial moratorium. That is why national eligibility cannot be treated as a Bali result, however straightforward the national ownership position may appear. For founders, the editorial point is simple but consequential: the activity’s transport scope and its national openness do not override the Bali PMA block. The registerable path therefore turns on location as well as the stated activity.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreigner cannot register this activity as PMA in Bali today.
